title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics, new Grafana dashboards for token cost/latency breakdowns, and tuned alerting rules to use token-normalized thresholds. Instrumentation includes tracing spans for KV cache hit/miss and model/route tags. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: customers need visibility into per-token cost and latency, and how KV cache behavior influences unit economics. This PR instruments token-level KV cache metrics, exposes token-normalized latency and cost breakdowns, ships Grafana dashboards, and updates alerting thresholds to reduce noisy alerts while preserving SLO sensitivity. Changes follow ENG-9123 and ENG-9245. Implementation details: 1) Metrics: add kv.cache.hit_count, kv.cache.miss_count, kv.cache.latency_ms (histogram), token.cost_per_token, token.latency_per_token (histograms + p50/p95/p99). Metrics are labeled by model, route, region, customer_tier. 2) Tracing: add spans for KV lookup and cache restore with tags for hit/miss, shard_id, and sequence_prefix_length. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for token-level cost breakdown (by model/route), cache hit-rate over time, 95th token-normalized latency heatmap. 4) Alerts: migrate existing latency alerts to token-normalized versions, add composite alert that combines token_latency_p95 > threshold AND cache_hit_rate < 80% to reduce false positives. 5) Docs/tests: docs/observability/kv_cache.md and unit/integration tests for metrics emission and dashboard generation. Rollout plan: feature flag rollout over two weeks starting with internal accounts and canary on dedicated clusters. Backwards compatible: metrics additive only. See commits and files_changed for details.
